proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a member of \(\mathfrak M\).  All limits and probabilities below are conditional on its deterministic complete baseline array.  Put
\[
w_q=2^{1-K_f}c_q,\qquad
\mu_{iq}(\beta)=E_\beta\{Y_{in}(q)\mid x_{in}\},\qquad
\varepsilon_{iq}=Y_{in}(q)-\mu_{iq}(\beta).
\tag{1}
\]
The moment functions in (1), and their derivatives needed below, are continuous and uniformly bounded on the compact set \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal K\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}arraywise\text{-}moment\text{-}regularity}\).  The empirical baseline measures converge by \(\mathrm{ass{:}baseline\text{-}limit}\), while \(\mathrm{ass{:}baseline\text{-}gram}\) keeps the imbalance covariance nonsingular on its effective range.  Therefore the empirical covariance matrices entering \(\mathcal B_T(\beta)\) converge, uniformly in \(\beta\), along the full array.  Continuity of the Moore--Penrose inverse on a constant-rank stratum, using \(\mathrm{ass{:}oracle\text{-}rank}\), gives
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left\|\mathcal B_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)
-\mathcal B_\infty(\beta)\right\|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{2}
\]
The same sampling-without-replacement variance calculation applied to each bounded moment function gives (2) in probability for a uniform complement of size \(N\to\infty\).  The derivative convergence in \(\mathrm{lem{:}experiment\text{-}indexed\text{-}oracle\text{-}convergence}\) identifies the normalization
\[
G_\infty(\beta)
=\frac{M_\beta}{\operatorname{tr}(M_\beta)},
\qquad
M_\beta
=\mathcal B_\infty(\beta)^{\mathsf T}
 W\mathcal B_\infty(\beta).
\tag{3}
\]
The denominator in (3) is positive.  Indeed, the full-array signal floor and (2) imply
\[
\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\operatorname{tr}(M_\beta)>0.
\tag{4}
\]
Uniform boundedness of the moments gives the corresponding finite upper bound.

We next calculate the leading oracle gain.  For a balanced set \(T\) of size \(k\), define the ordinary cell-contrast statistic
\[
\widetilde{\boldsymbol\tau}_T
=\frac{1}{k}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
Qw_q\mathbf 1\{Z_i=q\}Y_{in}(q).
\tag{5}
\]
Under complete randomization, \(\pi_{iq}=1/Q\), so (5) is exactly the Horvitz--Thompson estimator.  Apply
\(\mathrm{lem{:}balanced\text{-}random\text{-}partition\text{-}clt}\)
to the bounded deterministic vector containing all conditional means in (1) and all baseline coordinates.  The maximum-influence premise of that lemma follows from \(\mathrm{ass{:}baseline\text{-}bound}\) and the uniform bound on \(\mu_{iq}\).  After standardizing the nondegenerate imbalance coordinates, it yields jointly
\[
\left(
\sqrt{k}\{\widetilde{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\,\mu}_T
-\boldsymbol\tau_T^\mu\},
\sqrt{k}\Delta_T
\right)
\Rightarrow
\left(\mathcal B_\infty(\beta)Z+R,Z\right),
\tag{6}
\]
where \(Z\sim N(0,I_{Fp})\), \(R\) is centered Gaussian, and
\(\operatorname{Cov}(R,Z)=0\).  Joint Gaussianity then makes \(R\) independent of \(Z\).  This is a random-partition limit for the bounded deterministic conditional-mean table; it is not a Gaussian assertion about the outcome residuals.

Under \(p_{T,H}\), the Radon--Nikodym derivative with respect to balanced complete randomization is
\[
\eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}a_{T,H},
\tag{7}
\]
which is bounded by \(\eta+(1-\eta)/\alpha\).  Take \(H=G_T(\beta)\).  By
\(\mathrm{lem{:}experiment\text{-}indexed\text{-}oracle\text{-}convergence}\),
the quadratic score in the standardized version of (6) converges to
\(g_\beta(Z)\).  By
\(\mathrm{lem{:}gaussian\text{-}boundary\text{-}regularity}\),
\(g_\beta(Z)\) has no mass at \(q_{\alpha,\beta}\).  Hence the exact common randomization on a finite tie set has a vanishing contribution in the limit, and the lower-tail factor in (7) converges in \(L_1\) to
\[
\eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}
\mathbf 1\{g_\beta(Z)\leq q_{\alpha,\beta}\}.
\tag{8}
\]
The exact complete-randomization second-moment identity in the cited random-partition lemma gives convergence of the second moments in (6).  Multiplication by the uniformly bounded density (7) preserves uniform integrability.  Thus no fourth-moment assertion is needed to pass from (6)--(8) to quadratic risks.

The independent residual \(R\) has the same quadratic contribution before and after the tilt (8), because the tilt is measurable with respect to \(Z\).  The part explained by imbalance has loss
\[
Z^{\mathsf T}M_\beta Z
=\operatorname{tr}(M_\beta)g_\beta(Z).
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (6)--(9) therefore give for the deterministic conditional-mean table
\[
\begin{aligned}
&k\left\{
V_T^\mu(0,\beta)-V_T^\mu(G_T(\beta),\beta)
\right\}\\
&\quad\longrightarrow
(1-\eta)\operatorname{tr}(M_\beta)
\left[
E\{g_\beta(Z)\}
-\alpha^{-1}E\!\left\{
g_\beta(Z)\mathbf 1(g_\beta(Z)\leq q_{\alpha,\beta})
\right\}
\right]
=a(\beta).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]

It remains to verify that neither stochastic outcome noise nor exact unequal inclusions alter (10).  First, balanced complete randomization gives
\[
P(Z_i=q)=\frac1Q.
\tag{11}
\]
For the exact mixture,
\[
\pi_{iq}(T,G_T)
=\frac1Q\left[
\eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}
E_{\mathrm{CR}}\{a_{T,G_T}\mid Z_i=q\}
\right].
\tag{12}
\]
Conditioning on \(Z_i=q\) deletes one bounded unit and changes the standardized imbalance by \(O(k^{-1/2})\).  Apply the random-partition central limit theorem to the remaining \(k-1\) units.  The zero boundary mass used in (8) implies
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\max_{i\in T,q\in\mathcal Q}
\left|
E_{\mathrm{CR}}\{a_{T,G_T}\mid Z_i=q\}-\alpha
\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{13}
\]
Uniformity follows by contradiction: a failing sequence has, by compactness of \(\mathcal K\), a convergent parameter subsequence; bounded moment equicontinuity and (2) then reduce it to the pointwise leave-one-unit limit just proved.  From (12)--(13),
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\max_{i,q}
\left|\pi_{iq}(T,G_T)-\frac1Q\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{14}
\]
The same joint limit and the symmetry of the centered quadratic lower tail show that the ordinary statistic (5) has bias \(o(k^{-1/2})\) under (7).  Together with (14), the balanced identities
\(\sum_{i\in T}\pi_{iq}=k/Q\), and the exact second-moment bound of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}single\text{-}wave\text{-}risk}\), this gives
\[
\sqrt{k}\left(
\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(G_T)
-\widetilde{\boldsymbol\tau}_T
\right)\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in }L_2.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus exact inclusion weighting has no additional conditional-mean contribution to (10).

For completeness, its residual contribution can be checked without a limit theorem.  Put
\(\sigma_{i,qr}(\beta)=E_\beta(\varepsilon_{iq}\varepsilon_{ir}\mid x_{in})\).
Independence across units under \(\mathrm{ass{:}stable\text{-}product\text{-}law}\) removes every \(i\ne j\) term.  For the same unit and \(q\ne r\),
\[
E\left[
\left\{\frac{\mathbf 1(Z_i=q)}{\pi_{iq}}-1\right\}
\left\{\frac{\mathbf 1(Z_i=r)}{\pi_{ir}}-1\right\}
\right]=-1,
\tag{16}
\]
because a unit cannot receive two labels.  Hence all cross-treatment same-unit terms cancel when complete randomization is compared with the mixture.  The remaining diagonal difference is exactly
\[
\frac1{k^2}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
w_q^{\mathsf T}Ww_q\,\sigma_{i,qq}(\beta)
\left(Q-\frac1{\pi_{iq}(T,G_T)}\right).
\tag{17}
\]
The conditional variances are uniformly bounded by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}arraywise\text{-}moment\text{-}regularity}\); multiplying (17) by \(k\) and using (14) makes it converge uniformly to zero.  Combining (10), (15), and (17) proves
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}|k\,d_T(\beta)-a(\beta)|\longrightarrow0
\tag{18}
\]
along the full array.

For a uniform random complement with \(N\to\infty\), sampling-without-replacement variances for the bounded moment functions are \(O(N^{-1})\).  Therefore the preceding argument gives (18) in probability over the split.  Moreover,
\[
N|d_T(\beta)|
\leq N\{V_T(0,\beta)+V_T(G_T(\beta),\beta)\}\leq C
\tag{19}
\]
uniformly in \(\beta\), by
\(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}single\text{-}wave\text{-}risk}\) and the common conditional second-moment bound on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal K\).  The domination (19) upgrades convergence in probability to the asserted \(L_1(P_{S_m})\) convergence.

Finally, (2)--(4), the continuity of \(G_\infty\), and the zero-boundary-mass conclusion imply continuity of \(a\) by dominated convergence.  Because \(G_\infty\) has positive rank and trace one, \(g_\beta(Z)\) is nonconstant and nonnegative.  Since \(0<\alpha<1\),
\[
\alpha^{-1}E\!\left[
g_\beta(Z)\mathbf 1\{g_\beta(Z)\leq q_{\alpha,\beta}\}
\right]
<E\{g_\beta(Z)\}.
\tag{20}
\]
Equations (4) and (20), compactness of \(\mathcal K\), and \(0<\eta<1\) prove the displayed uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds for \(a\).

If \(m/n\to c\) and \(N\to\infty\), simple algebra gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&n\left[
d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}
-\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}
\right]\\
&\quad=
n\,d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}
-\frac Nn E_{S_m}\left[
N\,d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}
\right]
\longrightarrow a-(1-c)a=c\,a.
\end{aligned}
\tag{21}
\]
If \(c=1\) and \(N\) does not diverge, (19) makes the second term in (21) vanish; a subsequence argument covers mixtures of bounded and diverging \(N\).  The convergence is uniform in \(\beta\).  Nothing in (18) controls the cancellation error relative to \(m/n^2\) when \(m/n\to0\), so the frontier-scale deletion coefficient remains open exactly as stated.

Fix an interior point \(\beta_0\in\mathcal K^\circ\).  For any pilot-measurable action \(\delta_m\), combine the two terms involving the main oracle in the exact accounting identity:
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta_0)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta_0)
&=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta_0)\\
&\quad+\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E\!\left[
V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta_0)
-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(0,\beta_0)
\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{33}
\]
Identity (33) is exact: the two occurrences of the main-wave empirical oracle cancel algebraically.  Since every risk is nonnegative,
\[
V_T(\delta_m,\beta_0)-V_T(0,\beta_0)
\geq -V_T(0,\beta_0).
\tag{34}
\]
The fixed member has a finite common conditional second-moment envelope on
\(\mathcal X\times\mathcal K\) by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}arraywise\text{-}moment\text{-}regularity}\).  Therefore
\(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}single\text{-}wave\text{-}risk}\), applied with \(H=0\), gives a constant \(C<\infty\) such that
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}V_T(0,\beta)\leq\frac C{|T|}
\tag{35}
\]
for every balanced nonempty wave.  From (33)--(35),
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta_0)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta_0)
\geq d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta_0)-C\frac N{n^2}.
\tag{36}
\]
The repaired first-order gain theorem gives
\[
n\,d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta_0)\longrightarrow a(\beta_0)>0.
\tag{37}
\]
Because \(N=o(n)\), the last term in (36) is \(o(n^{-1})\).  Hence for all sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly over \(\delta_m\),
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta_0)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta_0)
\geq\frac{a(\beta_0)}{2n}>0.
\tag{38}
\]
By the definition of \(\mathcal E_n(m)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E_n(m)
&=\inf_{\delta_m}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left[R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)\right]_+\\
&\geq
\inf_{\delta_m}
\left[R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta_0)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta_0)\right]_+
\geq\frac{a(\beta_0)}{2n}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{39}
\]
Multiplying (39) by \(n^{3/2}\) proves the claim.  The proof uses only the nearly-all-pilot condition \(N=o(n)\); none of the other endpoint windows follows from (39).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(Q\) be fixed.  For each \(k\), let \(u_{1k},\ldots,u_{kk}\in\mathbb R^d\) be a deterministic finite population, let \(Q\mid k\), and assign exactly \(k/Q\) units to each of \(Q\) labels uniformly at random.  Write \(\bar u_k=k^{-1}\sum_i u_{ik}\), \(\bar u_{qk}=Qk^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_i=q}u_{ik}\), and \(S_k=(k-1)^{-1}\sum_i(u_{ik}-\bar u_k)(u_{ik}-\bar u_k)^{\mathsf T}\).  If \(S_k\to S\) and
\[
\frac{1}{k}\max_{i\leq k}\lVert u_{ik}-\bar u_k\rVert^2\longrightarrow0,
\]
then
\[
\sqrt{k}\bigl(\bar u_{1k}-\bar u_k,\ldots,\bar u_{Qk}-\bar u_k\bigr)
\ \Rightarrow\
N\!\left(0,\{QI_Q-\mathbf 1_Q\mathbf 1_Q^{\mathsf T}\}\otimes S\right).
\]
The conclusion holds jointly for any fixed finite collection of coordinates, and the corresponding randomization second moments converge to the displayed Gaussian second moments.

added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The split \(S_m\), the balanced treatment labels \(Z_{S_m}\), and all auxiliary randomizers have laws fixed by the design and hence do not depend on \(\beta\).  The baseline array is a point mass under \(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}baseline}\).  Conditional independence across units under \(\mathrm{ass{:}stable\text{-}product\text{-}law}\) therefore gives
\[
dP_\beta^{\mathcal O_m}
=dP(S_m,Z_{S_m})
\prod_{i\in S_m}
p_{Z_i,\beta}\{dY_{in}(Z_i)\mid x_{in}\}.
\tag{22}
\]
Taking the ratio of (22) at \(\beta_1\) and \(\beta_0\) cancels the parameter-free design factor and proves the displayed likelihood identity.  Differentiating its logarithm at \(\beta\), justified by \(\mathrm{ass{:}qmd}\), gives
\[
\Delta_m(\beta)
=\frac1{\sqrt m}\sum_{i\in S_m}
s_{Z_i,\beta}\{Y_{in}(Z_i)\mid x_{in}\}.
\tag{23}
\]
Each summand has conditional mean zero.  Independence of the observed outcomes conditional on \((\mathbf X_n,S_m,Z_{S_m})\) makes the conditional covariance of (23) exactly \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}(\beta;S_m,Z)\).  This proves the positive part of the audit.

We now give a certificate that the asserted convergence to \(I(\beta)\) is not a consequence of the frozen conditions.  Take \(p=1\), let the deterministic baselines alternate between
\[
-1+\frac1n
\quad\hbox{and}\quad
1+\frac1n,
\tag{24}
\]
and let \(\nu=\tfrac12\delta_{-1}+\tfrac12\delta_1\).  The array (24) is uniformly bounded, its empirical law converges weakly to \(\nu\), and its centered empirical variance converges to one, so the three baseline assumptions hold.  Define the bounded measurable function
\[
h(-1)=h(1)=1,
\qquad
h(x)=2\quad\hbox{for }x\notin\{-1,1\}.
\tag{25}
\]
For a nuisance coordinate \(\lambda\in[-1/48,1/48]\), put a residual variable on
\(\{-3,-1,1,3\}\) with probabilities
\[
P_\lambda(E=y_j\mid x)
=\frac14+\lambda h(x)v_j,
\qquad
v=(-1,3,-3,1).
\tag{26}
\]
All probabilities in (26) lie between \(1/8\) and \(3/8\), so domination, positivity, uniform quadratic-mean differentiability, and the uniform third score moment hold.  Direct calculation gives
\[
\sum_jv_j=0,\qquad
\sum_jy_jv_j=0,\qquad
\sum_jy_j^2v_j=0.
\tag{27}
\]
Thus the conditional first and second moments in this nuisance direction are constant in \((x,\lambda)\), notwithstanding the discontinuity of \(h\).  They satisfy both conditional-moment smoothness assumptions.  This nuisance factor may be combined with any bounded finite-support regular oracle component by using a sufficiently small independent residual scale; equations (27) leave its first two moment derivatives and hence its oracle map unchanged.  Enlarging the finite support if necessary gives a one-to-one bounded encoding of the two finite components.  The information matrix remains positive definite on a small product ball, while \(D_\lambda G_T=0\).  The oracle rank, signal, and curvature conditions of the original component persist under a sufficiently small bounded perturbation.  Hence this is a generic-class certificate within the stated model architecture, rather than a violation of an oracle assumption.

At \(\lambda=0\), the nuisance score in category \(j\) is
\[
s_{\lambda,j}(x)=4h(x)v_j,
\]
and its conditional Fisher information is
\[
\sum_{j=1}^4\frac14\{4h(x)v_j\}^2
=4h(x)^2\sum_{j=1}^4v_j^2
=80h(x)^2.
\tag{28}
\]
Every finite-\(n\) baseline in (24) lies outside \(\{-1,1\}\).  Therefore the nuisance--nuisance entry of \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}(0;S_m,Z)\) is exactly \(80\cdot2^2=320\), for every split and balanced assignment.  In contrast, (25) and the definition of \(I(\beta)\) give
\[
\frac1Q\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
\int80h(x)^2\,\nu(dx)=80.
\tag{29}
\]
Equations (28)--(29) prove the failure of information convergence.  The obstruction is precisely that weak convergence of the baseline empirical measure controls bounded continuous functions, whereas no frozen assumption makes
\(x\mapsto E_\beta(s_{q,\beta}s_{q,\beta}^{\mathsf T}\mid x)\)
continuous.  Thus replacing the random matrix \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}\) by \(I\), and any LAN-to-action conclusion using that replacement, would add an unstated hypothesis.

added_lemmas.statement:
Define the deletion contrast and the action-loss contrast by
\[
D_{n,m}(\beta)
=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)
-\left(\frac Nn\right)^2
E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)
\]
and
\[
L_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)
=\left(\frac Nn\right)^2
E\!\left[
V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta)
-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}
\{G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta\}
\right].
\]
Then, for every pilot-measurable action,
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
=D_{n,m}(\beta)+L_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta).
\]
The quantity \(L_{n,m}\) is a contrast and need not be nonnegative because the empirical Gaussian oracle is not assumed to minimize exact finite Horvitz--Thompson risk.  If \(s_{n,m}=m/n^2+1/(nm)\), the proposed second-order expansion for \(\widehat G_m\) is equivalent to
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\frac{\left|
\{D_{n,m}(\beta)-A(\beta)m/n^2\}
+\{L_{n,m}(\widehat G_m,\beta)-B(\beta)/(nm)\}
\right|}{s_{n,m}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Separate little-oh bounds for the two braced terms are sufficient but, without a no-cancellation premise, are not necessary.  Every proposed arbitrary-action lower bound is likewise exactly equivalent to the result obtained by substituting \(D_{n,m}+L_{n,m}\); there is no third cross-wave term.

Let \(\mathcal K\) be compact, let \(A,B:\mathcal K\to(0,\infty)\) be continuous, and define \(\Phi,t^\star,C^\star\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}global\text{-}envelope}\).  Suppose the following two deterministic premises hold:
\[
\sup_{\substack{m\in\mathcal M_n\\ a\leq m/\sqrt n\leq b}}
\left|n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)-\Phi(m/\sqrt n)\right|
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{for every }0<a<b<\infty,
\tag{40}
\]
and, for every sequence \(m_n\in\mathcal M_n\) with
\(m_n/\sqrt n\to0\) or \(m_n/\sqrt n\to\infty\),
\[
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m_n)\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{41}
\]
Then
\[
n^{3/2}\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)\longrightarrow C^\star>0.
\]
In particular, the denominator is positive for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Every sequence \(m_n\in\mathcal M_n\) satisfying
\[
\frac{\mathcal E_n(m_n)}
{\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)}
\longrightarrow1
\]
obeys
\[
\frac{m_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow t^\star,
\qquad
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m_n)\longrightarrow C^\star.
\]
The minimizer \(t^\star\) is unique, and
\[
C^\star
=\max_{(a,b)\in\operatorname{conv}
\{(A(\beta),B(\beta)):\beta\in\mathcal K\}}
2\sqrt{ab},
\]
with a certificate supported on at most two parameter values active at \(t^\star\).  This proposition is a conditional deterministic transfer and does not assert (40) or (41) for the statistical model.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because \(Q\) is fixed and \(Q\mid n\), for every fixed \(t>0\) there is, for all sufficiently large \(n\), a point \(m_n(t)\in\mathcal M_n\) satisfying
\[
\left|\frac{m_n(t)}{\sqrt n}-t\right|
\leq\frac Q{\sqrt n}.
\tag{42}
\]
Indeed, round \(t\sqrt n\) to the nearest multiple of \(Q\); for large \(n\) it lies between \(Q\) and \(n-Q\).  Choose a compact interval \([a,b]\) containing \(t\) in its interior.  Premise (40), continuity of \(\Phi\), and (42) give
\[
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n\{m_n(t)\}
\longrightarrow\Phi(t).
\tag{43}
\]
Taking \(t=t^\star\) proves
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
n^{3/2}\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)
\leq C^\star.
\tag{44}
\]

Let \(\ell_n\) be an exact minimizer over the finite nonempty set
\(\mathcal M_n\).  If \(\ell_n/\sqrt n\) were not eventually contained in some compact subinterval of \((0,\infty)\), a subsequence would have a further subsequence tending to zero or infinity.  Premise (41) would make the scaled risk diverge along that subsequence, contradicting the finite upper bound (44).  Hence there are \(0<a<b<\infty\) such that eventually
\[
a\leq\ell_n/\sqrt n\leq b.
\tag{45}
\]
Every subsequence has a further subsequence on which
\(\ell_n/\sqrt n\to\bar t\in[a,b]\).  Applying (40) on this compact window yields
\[
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\ell_n)
=\Phi(\ell_n/\sqrt n)+o(1)
\longrightarrow\Phi(\bar t)\geq C^\star.
\tag{46}
\]
Together, (44) and (46) prove
\[
n^{3/2}\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)
\longrightarrow C^\star.
\tag{47}
\]

Continuity and strict positivity of \(A\) and \(B\) on compact
\(\mathcal K\) give constants \(A_->0\) and \(B_->0\).  Thus
\[
\Phi(t)\geq A_-t+\frac{B_-}{t}
\geq2\sqrt{A_-B_-}>0,
\tag{48}
\]
so \(C^\star>0\).  Equation (47) consequently implies positivity of the unscaled denominator for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Now let \(m_n\) satisfy the displayed asymptotic-minimax ratio.  Equations (43), (47), and the ratio condition show that
\[
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m_n)\longrightarrow C^\star.
\tag{49}
\]
Premise (41) and (49) localize \(m_n/\sqrt n\) to a compact subinterval of \((0,\infty)\), by the same subsequence argument used for (45).  If a subsequence converges to \(\widetilde t\), premise (40) and (49) imply
\[
\Phi(\widetilde t)=C^\star.
\tag{50}
\]
The uniqueness conclusion of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}deterministic\text{-}envelope\text{-}certificate}\)
makes \(\widetilde t=t^\star\).  Every convergent subsequence has this same limit, so \(m_n/\sqrt n\to t^\star\).  The convex-hull formula and the at-most-two-active-parameter certificate are exactly the remaining conclusions of that established lemma.  This proves every assertion as an implication from (40)--(41).

added_lemmas.statement: Given the exact pilot likelihood and its random information matrix \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}\), can one formulate and prove a valid subsequential LAN experiment indexed by an actual limit of \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}\), and then transfer its Gaussian decision bound to the exact finite Horvitz--Thompson action-loss contrast uniformly over arbitrary pilot-measurable actions?  Any positive answer must also prove localization, quadratic-loss uniform integrability, and the finite moving-boundary comparison; it may not replace \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}\) by \(I\) under the present assumptions.

Does the statistical model \(\mathfrak M\) establish both premises of \(\mathrm{prop{:}balanced\text{-}grid\text{-}argmin\text{-}transfer}\) with the candidate functions \(A\) and \(B\)?  Concretely, can one prove the compact-window limit
\[
\sup_{\substack{m\in\mathcal M_n\\ a\leq m/\sqrt n\leq b}}
\left|n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)
-\max_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\{A(\beta)m/\sqrt n+B(\beta)\sqrt n/m\}\right|
\longrightarrow0
\]
for every \(0<a<b<\infty\), together with sequential coercivity for bounded pilots, \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\), positive pilot fractions with \(N\asymp n\), and \(N=o(n)\)? prose_updates.tldr: A balanced pilot and a positive-support exact-alpha main-wave mixture retain exact Horvitz--Thompson centering for the realized finite-population factorial vector.  The proved contribution is now an exact two-component risk identity, a first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain limit, and exclusion of the nearly-all-pilot endpoint.  The pilot likelihood factors exactly through revealed outcomes, but its realized information matrix need not converge to the population matrix under the current baseline assumptions.  A unique square-root pilot constant follows from a proved deterministic balanced-grid argmin proposition only if compact-window second-order convergence and endpoint coercivity are established.  Those statistical premises, including exact ties, unequal inclusions, arbitrary actions, and the nuisance-information bridge, remain open.

project_justification.gap: Existing factorial rerandomization theory supplies first-order Gaussian precision and existing two-wave work supplies accounting architecture, but neither proves a moving-boundary exact Horvitz--Thompson comparison at the square-root pilot scale.  The present information audit also shows that the stated moment conditions do not identify the pilot Fisher-information limit.
project_justification.niche: On a fixed complete baseline array with a full-dimensional product parameter domain, the design problem separates exactly into a deletion contrast and a potentially signed action-loss contrast.  This exposes, rather than assumes, the two finite-randomization bridges needed for sharp pilot sizing.
project_justification.fill: The note proves exact pooled Horvitz--Thompson accounting, the explicit first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain coefficient, the exact pilot likelihood and realized information matrix, a nearly-all-pilot lower bound, and a conditional deterministic argmin certificate.  It leaves the frontier coefficients and the global statistical pilot theorem as explicit open questions.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional on the selected pilot identities and balanced labels, only the revealed outcomes contribute to the likelihood.  Their score covariance is the random matrix \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}\).  The current assumptions do not imply convergence of this matrix to \(I(\beta)\), so nuisance-efficient estimation and its transfer to exact action loss are conditional proof goals rather than established features.

prose_updates.related_work: Han and Deng provide the closest factorial sample-splitting architecture and first-order oracle equivalence; their results inform the present first-order comparison but do not supply the deletion cancellation or exact moving-boundary action loss.  Li and Ding provide the random-partition central limit theorem used for the bounded conditional-mean table.  Li, Ding, and Rubin provide the symmetric truncated-Gaussian predecessor, now recorded only as informing the unresolved finite-boundary question because the present design permits ties and unequal inclusions.  Yamin provides the deterministic compact-localization and argmin-transfer architecture, not the statistical square-root rate or its coefficients.  Armstrong's LAN efficiency bounds become relevant only after an actual pilot-information limit is available.  Horvitz and Thompson support exact inverse-inclusion centering, while the remaining rerandomization and consistency papers do not close the second-order exact-risk comparison.  Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella motivate sequential factorial replications, but no pilot-size recommendation is certified until the two open statistical premises are proved.
prose_updates.interpretation: For planning, the proved coefficient \(a(\beta)\) quantifies the first-order loss from deleting a macroscopic fraction of units for learning, and the nearly-all-pilot result rules out leaving only a sublinear main wave.  The familiar balance \(A t+B/t\) is presently a conditional design calculation, not a validated sample-size rule for this experiment.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Exact score orderings can jump on deterministic lattices and exact inclusion probabilities can be unequal.  The first-order proof absorbs these effects through zero Gaussian boundary mass, leave-one-unit inclusion convergence, and exact residual covariance cancellation.  These arguments do not provide the finer remainder needed when \(m/n\to0\).  Separately, smooth first and second outcome moments do not control score information as a function of the baseline, so the pilot LAN information cannot be fixed at \(I(\beta)\) without additional derivation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established results are exact Horvitz--Thompson centering and accounting, the one-wave risk bound, common oracle-map convergence, Gaussian boundary regularity, the first-order exact-mixture oracle gain, the exact pilot likelihood and information audit, the nearly-all-pilot exclusion, and the conditional deterministic envelope transfer.  The coefficient \(A\) remains an unresolved deletion candidate and \(B\) remains a Gaussian action candidate.  Uniform frontier-scale deletion, exact finite action curvature, arbitrary-action localization, information convergence, the remaining endpoint windows, and the unconditional global pilot rule are open.  The causal estimand remains the fixed realized factorial vector throughout.
